title: Choose MealOS’s visual world
question: Choose the world that should make MealOS feel at home on your Fold8 Ultra, or re-roll the hand.

options.label: Butcher-Paper Prep Map
options.lineage: butcher paper prep plans and grease-pencil kitchen marks
options.thesis: One continuous working sheet turns a week of meals into a clear prep map.
options.viewport: An unfolded working sheet divided evenly at the hinge: a large active step at left, measured ingredients and live timers at right, with the week traced along the top edge.
options.risk: Can feel rustic if the typography and controls are not unmistakably modern Android.

raised.raise: Timer states become unmistakable, high-contrast events instead of quiet metadata.
Hierarchy relies on disciplined scale before decoration.
The paper world fully occupies the screen rather than appearing as a card theme.
Fold and unfold preserve one continuous cooking state.
Every active tool and ingredient receives an explicit label.

options.label: Mise en Place Board
options.lineage: a cook’s organized prep station before service
options.thesis: Everything needed for the next action is visibly in its place.
options.viewport: Two equal work zones sit on one calm prep surface: the current step and progression at left, ingredients and two tactile timers at right, with compact destinations tucked into an adaptive rail.
options.risk: This is the most immediately usable direction, but also the one most likely to become a familiar premium recipe app.

options.label: Kitchen Line Map
options.thesis: Meals become routes: prep, cook, rest, and serve are stations on a legible line.
options.viewport: An equal two-pane cooking view uses a bold route line to connect the active step, appliance timer, and next action while ingredients remain a labeled station list.
options.case: It makes progress and multi-timer dependencies unusually clear, while requiring more learning than the grounded kitchen worlds.
options.risk: The route metaphor could add cognitive load during a simple recipe if every screen performs it.

options.label: Nixie Kitchen Counter
options.thesis: Cooking time becomes the physical center of the interface.
options.viewport: Large glass timers anchor the cooking view while steps and ingredients sit on engraved instrument panels.
options.case: The timer story is superb, but weekly planning and grocery work do not naturally belong to the instrument panel.
options.kept: Timer states become unmistakable, high-contrast events.
options.risk: Dark laboratory hardware can feel clinical and visually heavy in a kitchen.

options.label: Continuous Fold
options.thesis: One unbroken surface carries the recipe through every device posture.
options.viewport: An equal two-pane sheet meets at a deliberate crease, with steps advancing like numbered folds.
options.case: The continuity is relevant, but a literal fold metaphor competes with the food and is culturally disconnected from the meal rotation.
options.kept: Fold and unfold preserve one continuous cooking state.
options.risk: The visual metaphor risks becoming the subject instead of the meal.

options.label: Measured Type Specimen
options.thesis: Scale alone separates what to do now from everything supporting it.
options.viewport: One enormous instruction balances a strict ingredient column and precise timer readouts.
options.case: The hierarchy is excellent, but the system does not naturally express meal identity, shopping categories, or warmth.
options.kept: Hierarchy relies on disciplined scale before decoration.
options.risk: Could feel editorial and austere rather than useful in a busy kitchen.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: a surreal quarry of cut weather blocks
options.thesis: Meals assemble from visible blocks that transform from raw to ready.
options.viewport: Large ingredient blocks cross a central seam as the current recipe is assembled.
options.case: The transformation story is memorable, but it obscures familiar food and demands imagery the utility does not need.
options.kept: The chosen material world fully occupies the screen.
options.risk: Visual spectacle would outrank speed and clarity.

options.label: Kitchen Cutaway
options.thesis: Every appliance and ingredient is visible doing its job in one continuous kitchen.
options.viewport: The unfolded device becomes a labeled cutaway kitchen with the active recipe moving from tool to tool.
options.case: It identifies every object clearly, but its playful illustrated scene conflicts with quick adult utility.
options.kept: Every active tool and ingredient receives an explicit label.
options.risk: Likely too playful for an everyday planning tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished Material 3 meal planner with recipe photography, familiar cards, and standard navigation.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional two-pane list-detail screen with recipe cards, a large food image, ingredients, and a floating start-cooking action.
canonCard.risk: Immediately familiar, but visually interchangeable with many existing recipe apps.
